text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Housing and New Communities Minister Mohamed Ibrahim Soleiman said the cabinet was looking at the final details of planning 42 new towns to take 20 million people, the extra population expected by the year 2020.
- The government has decided to spend 222 million pounds ($65 million) on sports activities over the next three years.
- Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro will start a two-day official visit to Egypt from Friday.
- Provincial governors will today discuss the effects of the floods and violations of building regulations.

- Local Government Minister Mahmoud Sherif attended the signing of a deal to set up a tourist complex at Qantara East on the Suez Canal at a cost of two billion pounds from Egyptian and Kuwaiti investors.

- Police have recovered a statue of Isis stolen from the open-air museum at Memphis. Three armed men in masks raided the museum 10 days ago, sawed up the statue and took it away in a car to sell it abroad for one million pounds. Police have arrested the three men.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said the government was taking special measures to solve the problem of unemployment and create more jobs for youngsters. He said all the incentives to investors are meant to encourage them to create jobs.
- The military court in Assiut sentenced four men to life imprisonment and two men to 15 years with hard labour for smuggling weapons from Sudan for sale to Islamist militants.
- Digging of the Sheikh Zaid canal will start at the beginning of next month. The giant irrigation station to serve the agricultural project will be put to international tender.

- Diplomatic sources said the discovery of two Israeli spy networks in Egypt in recent days had a negative effect on the atmosphere of trust supposedly created between the two countries after they signed a peace treaty.
